prompt:
Find what the Node.js project officially says about the lifecycle of its LTS releases (how long Active LTS and Maintenance LTS last). Cite the official page and quote it.

Output format (required):
For every claim you attribute to a source, write one line in exactly this form:
SOURCE: <full URL> | QUOTE: "<a sentence copied word-for-word from that page>" | CLAIM: <what you take it to show>
For anything the task asks about that you could not find a source for, write one line:
NO_SOURCE_FOUND: <what you could not find>
You can write normal explanation before or after these lines.

response.content:
The Node.js project defines its Long Term Support (LTS) lifecycle through a structured schedule managed by the Release Working Group. According to the official documentation, an LTS release typically enters an "Active LTS" phase for 12 months, followed by a "Maintenance LTS" phase for 18 months, resulting in a total support duration of 30 months from the initial LTS start date.

SOURCE: https://github.com/nodejs/Release/blob/main/README.md | QUOTE: "Each LTS line is supported for 30 months beginning with the date it enters LTS." | CLAIM: The total duration of support for any given LTS release line is 30 months.

SOURCE: https://github.com/nodejs/Release/blob/main/README.md | QUOTE: "The first 12 months are called Active LTS and the remaining 18 months are called Maintenance LTS." | CLAIM: The 30-month lifecycle is divided into a 12-month Active LTS period and an 18-month Maintenance LTS period.
